newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Fresh violence flares in West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Fresh violence flares in West Bank.

text.p: Stone-throwing Palestinians kept up their street battles with Israeli soldiers on Sunday as Israel prepared for possible violence by its own Arab citizens on an annual protest day against land expropriation.

The killing of a Palestinian by Israeli troops on Saturday -- which a Palestinian cabinet minister called an act of war -- raised tensions after 10 days of clashes in the West Bank over Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

On Sunday, Israeli soldiers fired rubber bullets and teargas at hundreds of Palestinians who broke through Palestinian police lines to charge a Jewish settlement near the West Bank town of Jenin, witnesses said.
Scattered protests by stone-throwing Palestinians erupted in other West Bank areas but no serious injuries were reported.
In Gaza, hundreds of Palestinian youths tried to march on an Israeli checkpoint but were held back by Palestinian police, witnesses said.
The White House said on Friday that special envoy Dennis Ross's two-day Israeli-PLO crisis mission to the Middle East had been "constructive" but far more work remained.
An Easter message by Michel Sabbah, Latin Patriarch in Jerusalem, focused on "the evil around us" as the Palestinian Authority sounded a warning that the peace process was heading towards collapse.
"Blood is still unfortunately being shed," Sabbah said in a written message. "Violence is still in the heart and blindness concerning the rights of others is still in the minds of leaders."

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called on Israeli Arabs to shun violence on "Land Day" on Sunday, the annual commemoration of the 1976 killing by Israeli security forces of six Arabs protesting against expropriation of land by the government.

"I hope there will be quiet and I hope there will be no violence and I am using this opportunity also to say to the Arab citizens of Israel to keep calm and act within the framework of the law," he said late on Saturday.
Israeli police sent reinforcements to areas near Arab towns and villages. The Israeli army and paramilitary border police have already beefed up their forces in the West Bank.
Soldiers patrolled streets of Israeli cities, on alert for suicide bombers nine days after a Moslem militant killed himself and three Israeli women in an attack on a cafe in Tel Aviv.

Hundreds of mourners marched in a funeral procession on Sunday for Abdullah Khalil Abdullah, 20, killed by Israeli gunfire on Saturday in clashes on the outskirts of the self-ruled town of Ramallah, north of Jerusalem.

"No surrender," read one banner. Abdullah's body, held aloft by mourners, was wrapped in a Palestinian flag. A Palestinian police jeep covered with wreaths led the procession in Beit Sahour, near Bethlehem.
"This killing is a declaration of war," Palestinian Authority Finance Minister Mohammed Nashashibi said on Saturday.

Abdullah was the first Palestinian killed in the clashes. His home village of Beit Sahour is next to Jabal Abu Ghneim, known as Har Homa in Hebrew, the site where Israel broke ground for a settlement of 6,500 homes for Jews.
On Saturday, 24 Palestinians were wounded by Israeli rubber bullets and two by live ammunition, Arab hospital officials said.

The Palestinian Authority issued a plea on Saturday to the United States and Europe "to save the peace process from possible collapse". The Authority earlier rejected Netanyahu's conditions for resuming peace talks.
Netanyahu, after meeting Ross, the U.S. envoy, on Friday, said Palestinian President Yasser Arafat must arrest militants, dismantle guerrilla groups and tighten security cooperation.
Palestinians say work on the settlement must be halted as it pre-empts the results of negotiations yet to be held in final peace talks on Jerusalem's status.
Arafat went to meet Arab League foreign ministers on Sunday in Cairo, where a PLO official said all countries must cut ties with Israel because it had abandoned the peace process.

"We demand that all (Israeli) offices be shut, all international ties suspended, all political activities halted and we demand that particularly from Europe and the United States as sponsors of the peace process," Farouk Kaddoumi, head of the PLO's political affairs department, told reporters.
